result:
Not a git repo, so no diff available, but I've directly verified each edit via Read/Edit tool outputs. Summary of the fix:

**`src/lib/soft-delete.ts`** — added `NotArchivedError`/`assertArchived`, mirroring the existing `AlreadyArchivedError`/`assertNotArchived`, so restoring a live project is a domain-level conflict.

**`src/lib/errors.ts`** — mapped `NotArchivedError` to a `conflict` response, same as `AlreadyArchivedError`.

**`src/lib/slug.ts`** — added `uniqueKey()`, the key-space analogue of `uniqueSlug()`, suffixing collisions and trimming to 4 characters.

**`src/server/repositories/project-repository.ts`**:
- `countProjects` now actually filters to live projects (previously ignored its scope and counted archived rows too — the cause of "plan allows 2 projects" even after archiving one).
- `listTakenProjectSlugs` now includes archived projects (an archived project's address stays reserved) instead of treating it as free.
- added `listTakenProjectKeys` (same, archived included).
- `insertProject` now de-dupes both slug and key against those taken sets.
- `updateProject` now actually persists `status` (previously silently dropped).

**`src/server/services/project-service.ts`**:
- `restoreProject` now requires the project to actually be archived (`assertArchived`) and re-checks the plan's project quota before restoring, refusing and announcing nothing when either fails.
- `updateProject` refuses to mark a project `completed` while it has open issues (recomputed via existing `getProjectStats`), except when it's already completed (no-op).

**`src/server/services/usage-service.ts`** — added the missing `project.restored` listener incrementing `projectsUsed`, so the usage meter follows restores immediately instead of waiting for the periodic recount.

**`src/server/services/issue-service.ts`** — `createIssue` now refuses when the project isn't `active` (paused/completed projects reject new issues; existing issues are untouched).

**`src/actions/projects/create-project.ts`** — corrected the stale comment that justified counting archived projects against the quota.

I verified all 617 existing tests plus `tsc --noEmit` pass, and wrote a throwaway script (run via `tsx`, then deleted) exercising every scenario from the six support reports end-to-end — all behaved per the expected-behaviour spec.
